newsitem.title: CHINA: China to tighten grip on pension funds.
newsitem.headline: China to tighten grip on pension funds.

text.p: China will tighten control on management of pension funds to protect the interests of ordinary workers and curb investment risks, the China Securities said on Thursday.

China would put management of pension funds strictly under the state budget in the long-term and curb abuses in the short-term, it said, quoting Du Jian, head of the Social Insurance Department of the Ministry of Finance.
China's pension funds totalled 51.1 billion yuan at the end of 1995, of which 9.6 billion yuan was invested in treasury bonds and 3.16 billion yuan was deposited in state banks, he said.
Pension funds should be invested in low-risk treasury bonds to guarantee their safe returns, he said.
However, most of China's pension funds were invested in infrastructure projects, loaned to firms and even lent to individual investors and many funds failed to recover their investment.
The unauthorised investment and excessive spending by some fund managers were eroding basic insurance cover on ordinary workers, he said.
Ministry officials declined to give further details.
